rics.description: LSEG / Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index (PCSI)
rics.meaning: LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index.
rics.how_to_use: Alternative consumer sentiment gauge. Less market-watched than UMich/CB.

rics.description: Composite consumer confidence indicator
rics.meaning: Composite Consumer Confidence Indicator (OECD-standardized) — averages multiple confidence gauges into one international-comparison number.
rics.how_to_use: Use for cross-country comparisons. US-domestic analysts use UMich (aUSCSIUM) and Conference Board (aUSCONCF/A) directly. OECD composite smooths divergences between national surveys.

rics.description: National, Housing Affordability Index, composite
rics.meaning: National Housing Affordability Index — composite. NAR.
rics.how_to_use: 100 = median family can afford median home. Below 100 = affordability stress. Hit ~95 in 2023 — record low.

rics.description: National, Housing Affordability Index, median family income
rics.meaning: National Housing Affordability Index — median family income input. The denominator that scales the affordability calculation.
rics.how_to_use: Used to compute aUSHAI (affordability index = 100 means median family can afford median home). Tracks median family income trend; rises with NFP wages and demographic shifts.

rics.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, Reuters
rics.meaning: Mislabeled volume index — Reuters consumer surveys.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check raw source before using.

rics.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, Reuters
rics.meaning: Mislabeled volume index — Reuters consumer surveys.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check raw source.

rics.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, Reuters
rics.meaning: Mislabeled volume index — Reuters consumer surveys.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check raw source.

rics.description: Reuters poll: TR US IPSOS - Actual
rics.meaning: Reuters/Ipsos US Consumer Index — alternative consumer-mood gauge. Smaller-sample monthly survey by Ipsos.
rics.how_to_use: Tertiary cross-check vs UMich and Conference Board. Less market-moving on release. Useful when major confidence gauges diverge — provides third opinion.

rics.description: RCM/TIPP, Economic Optimism Index
rics.meaning: RCM/TIPP Economic Optimism Index — monthly investor and consumer optimism gauge published by Investor's Business Daily and TechnoMetrica. Combines six-month outlook, personal financial outlook, and confidence in federal economic policies.
rics.how_to_use: Smaller-sample alternative to UMich and Conference Board surveys. Use as a tertiary cross-check — when all three confidence gauges move in the same direction, the signal is robust; divergences are usually noise.

rics.description: Average consumer expectations, business & economic conditions
rics.meaning: Conference Board: average consumer expectations for business and economic conditions — composite expectations gauge from CB survey.
rics.how_to_use: Captures the forward-looking aggregate of CB consumer survey. More predictive than CB Present Situation. Pair with CB Expectations sub-index for full forward-look picture.

rics.description: Conference Board, Consumer confidence
rics.meaning: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index — survey of ~3,000 US households on present situation and future expectations. Released last Tuesday of each month.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with UMich sentiment — they sometimes diverge (CB more labor-market sensitive, UMich more inflation/wealth sensitive). The Expectations sub-index leads recessions: a >20pt YoY drop is a historical warning. Less market-moving on release than NFP/CPI.

rics.description: Conference Board, Consumer confidence, expectations
rics.meaning: Conference Board Consumer Confidence — Expectations sub-index. The forward-looking component, sub-80 typically signals recession.
rics.how_to_use: More predictive than the headline. >20pt YoY drop is recession-warning. Historically the cleaner of the two CB sub-indices for cycle calls.

rics.description: Conference Board, Consumer confidence, present situation
rics.meaning: Conference Board Consumer Confidence — Present Situation sub-index. Current-conditions assessment.
rics.how_to_use: Lags Expectations in turning points. Stays elevated longer at cycle peaks. Use the spread (Present − Expectations) as a recession-risk signal: when Present is high but Expectations falling fast, the cycle is rolling over.

rics.description: Conference Board, Future business conditions, better
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future business conditions, % of respondents saying 'better'. Bullish-expectations percentage.
rics.how_to_use: Forward-looking optimism share. Pair with 'worse' (aUSFBUSCW/A) for the diffusion (better − worse) used in net-confidence calculations. Falling 'better' share is recession-leading.

rics.description: Conference Board, Future business conditions, same
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future business conditions, % saying 'same'. Neutral/ambivalent percentage.
rics.how_to_use: Track for indecision share — typically the largest bucket. Stable at ~50-60% in normal times. Spikes during turning-point ambiguity.

rics.description: Conference Board, Future business conditions, worse
rics.meaning: CB future business conditions, % saying 'worse'.
rics.how_to_use: Bearish-expectations percentage. Sustained rises signal recession risk.

rics.description: Conference Board, Future employment, fewer jobs
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future employment, % expecting fewer jobs. Bearish labor-outlook percentage.
rics.how_to_use: Rises sharply ahead of recessions — one of CB's most reliable recession-leading sub-indices. Sustained >25% has preceded every recession since the survey began.

rics.description: Conference Board, Future employment, more jobs
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future employment, % expecting more jobs. Bullish labor-outlook percentage.
rics.how_to_use: Falling 'more jobs' share is recession-leading. Compute (more − fewer) for the labor-expectations diffusion — historically a reliable cycle signal.

rics.description: Conference Board, Future employment, same
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future employment, % expecting same number of jobs. Stability/uncertainty percentage.
rics.how_to_use: Largest bucket typically. Useful for tracking expectations volatility — when this share falls, respondents are taking strong views (bullish or bearish).

rics.description: Conference Board, Future income, decrease
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future income, % expecting decrease. Pessimistic income-outlook share.
rics.how_to_use: Income-expectations are the cleanest predictor of consumption. Rising 'decrease' share precedes consumption slowdowns. Track alongside real wage growth (aUSEARNW/CA).

rics.description: Conference Board, Future income, increase
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future income, % expecting increase. Optimistic income-outlook share.
rics.how_to_use: Falling income-optimism share is consumption-leading. The (increase − decrease) diffusion is the meaningful signal for forward consumption.

rics.description: Conference Board, Future income, same
rics.meaning: Conference Board: future income, % expecting same. Stability share — neutral income outlook.
rics.how_to_use: Largest bucket typically. Useful for tracking respondent confidence in projections.

rics.description: Conference Board, Plans to buy car within six months, yes
rics.meaning: Conference Board: plans to buy car within 6 months. Forward-looking auto-demand indicator from household survey.
rics.how_to_use: Leads auto sales by 1-3 months. Sustained drops below 4% historically signal slowing auto demand. Pair with aUSMAPPL6 (appliances) for big-ticket-durables outlook.

rics.description: Conference Board, Plans to buy major appliances within six months
rics.meaning: Conference Board: plans to buy major appliances within 6 months. Forward-looking durable-goods demand indicator.
rics.how_to_use: Big-ticket appliance demand follows housing-purchase activity. Falls when housing slows. Useful as a cross-check for retail sales of furniture/appliances (aUSRSLSHF/A).

rics.description: Conference Board, Present business conditions, bad
rics.meaning: Conference Board: present business conditions, % saying 'bad'. Pessimistic share for current-state assessment.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks present-conditions worry. Stays low in expansions; rises sharply at recession onset. (Good − bad) diffusion is the headline 'present situation' input.

rics.description: Conference Board, Present business conditions, good
rics.meaning: Conference Board: present business conditions, % saying 'good'. Optimistic share for current state.
rics.how_to_use: Stays elevated in expansions, drops sharply at recession onset. The (good − bad) diffusion is the CB Present Situation input. Falling 'good' share with rising 'bad' is a turning-point signal.

rics.description: Conference Board, Present business conditions, normal
rics.meaning: Conference Board: present business conditions, % saying 'normal'. Neutral share — middle of the distribution.
rics.how_to_use: Largest bucket. Tracks 'how typical' respondents see conditions. Movements between 'normal' and 'good'/'bad' show inflection-point dynamics.

rics.description: Conference Board, Present employment, jobs hard to get
rics.meaning: CB present employment, % saying jobs hard to get.
rics.how_to_use: Cleanest household-survey labor read. Rising = labor market loosening.

rics.description: Conference Board, Present employment, jobs not so plentiful
rics.meaning: Conference Board: present employment, % saying 'jobs not so plentiful'. Middle-position labor-market view.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks ambiguity in labor-market perception. Pair with 'jobs plentiful' and 'jobs hard to get' for full Conference Board labor differential calculation.

rics.description: Conference Board, Present employment, jobs plentiful
rics.meaning: Conference Board: present employment, % saying 'jobs plentiful'. Bullish labor-market view.
rics.how_to_use: Used in 'labor-market differential' calculation: (jobs plentiful − jobs hard to get). One of the most predictive labor-market indicators — leads the unemployment rate by 1-2 months.

rics.description: Consumer confidence
rics.meaning: Consumer confidence (standardized) — OECD-comparable consumer confidence framing. Aggregates multiple US confidence series.
rics.how_to_use: Use for cross-country comparisons. Domestic analysts use UMich/Conference Board directly. The standardization aligns with OECD methodology.

rics.description: Consumer Expectations Index
rics.meaning: Consumer Expectations Index (UMich).
rics.how_to_use: UMich forward-looking sub-index. Most market-relevant of UMich subseries.

rics.description: Consumer Sentiment Index
rics.meaning: Consumer Sentiment Index (UMich) headline.
rics.how_to_use: UMich headline sentiment. More inflation-sensitive than Conference Board.

rics.description: Current Conditions Index
rics.meaning: UMich Current Economic Conditions Index — present-state component of UMich monthly sentiment survey. Reflects current finances and buying-conditions assessments.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with UMich Expectations (aUSCONCFEX) for the headline sentiment. Current Conditions tends to lag Expectations at turning points; the gap (Conditions − Expectations) is a useful cycle indicator.

rics.description: Current Conditions Index-prelim
rics.meaning: UMich Current Economic Conditions — preliminary release (mid-month). Final release follows 2 weeks later.
rics.how_to_use: Markets trade the preliminary release. ~80% of months see no revision; large revisions (>3 points) signal late-month news (gas-price moves, geopolitical events).

rics.description: Total-prelim, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers
rics.meaning: UMich total preliminary headline.
rics.how_to_use: Mid-month headline preliminary release.

rics.description: Total-prelim, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers
rics.meaning: UMich preliminary expectations sub-index.
rics.how_to_use: Mid-month forward-looking preliminary.

rics.description: Total-prelim, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers
rics.meaning: UMich preliminary sentiment sub-index.
rics.how_to_use: Mid-month sentiment preliminary.

rics.description: U Mich 1Yr Inf Final
rics.meaning: UMich 1-year inflation expectation, final.
rics.how_to_use: Most-watched short-term inflation gauge. Fed monitors closely.

rics.description: U Mich 5-Yr Inf Final, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: UMich 5-year inflation expectation, final.
rics.how_to_use: Long-term anchor. Sub-3% = anchored; spikes signal Fed credibility risk.

rics.description: U Mich 5-Yr Inf Prelim, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: UMich 5-10 year median inflation expectations, preliminary release. Same conceptual measure as aUSINFEXM5Y at preliminary frequency.
rics.how_to_use: Markets watch the preliminary release for any change in long-term anchored expectations. Sustained moves above 3.5% in this preliminary print historically draw Fed attention; revisions in the final release can move markets if direction reverses.

rics.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, 1 Year Inflation Expectations (median)
rics.meaning: University of Michigan 1-year-ahead median inflation expectation — household survey response to 'how much do you expect prices to go up over the next 12 months?' One of the Fed's most-watched short-horizon expectations measures.
rics.how_to_use: Spikes when gasoline prices move (households over-weight what they see at the pump). The Fed cares about whether expectations stay 'anchored' — sustained moves above 4-5% raise concerns about a wage-price spiral. Cross-check against TIPS breakevens and NY Fed SCE.

rics.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, 5 Year Inflation Expectations (median)
rics.meaning: University of Michigan 5-10 year median inflation expectation — household long-horizon expectation. The Fed's primary anchored-expectations gauge from the household side.
rics.how_to_use: More stable than the 1Y series — typically pinned in a 2.5-3.5% band. Sustained moves above 3.5% are taken seriously by the FOMC; Powell has cited this series specifically in press conferences. Compare to 5Y5Y forward TIPS breakevens for a market-vs-survey read.

rics.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, Consumer Expectations Index
rics.meaning: UMich Consumer Expectations sub-index — forward-looking component of UMich sentiment.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with Conf Board Expectations (aUSCONCE/A). When both are falling together, recession risk is meaningful. UMich expectations weighed heavily by inflation; CB expectations weighed by labor market.

rics.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, Consumer Sentiment Index
rics.meaning: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index — headline. More inflation-sensitive than Conference Board. Twice-monthly release: preliminary mid-month, final end of month.
rics.how_to_use: The 1Y and 5-10Y inflation expectations sub-questions are Fed-monitored. UMich sentiment correlated with retail spending leads by 1-2 months. UMich + Conf Board divergences usually resolve toward UMich within 2-3 months.

rics.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, Current Conditions Index
rics.meaning: UMich Current Conditions Index — alternate.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check with aUSUMCRAPH.
